eyebrow: The distinction PIM is built around

steps.label: Eligible assignment
steps.sub: can activate the role on demand, for a bounded window — doesn't hold it continuously

steps.label: Active assignment
steps.sub: holds the role right now, exactly like a classic permanent assignment

steps.label: The goal
steps.sub: almost nobody permanently active on Owner, User Access Administrator, or Global Administrator

code:
# Per-role PIM activation settings:
#  - Require Azure MFA at activation       (on by default)
#  - Require a justification text entry
#  - Require approval from a designated approver
#  - Maximum activation duration             (hours, not indefinite)
#  - Notify specified reviewers on activation
#
# Assignment-time settings (separate):
#  - Require approval to BECOME eligible
#  - Eligible assignments expire after N days
caption: Activation and assignment each have their own, independently configured requirements.

steps.label: PIM for Entra ID roles
steps.sub: Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator — under Entra ID > Roles and administrators

steps.label: PIM for Azure resource roles
steps.sub: Owner, Contributor, custom roles — under Privileged Identity Management > Azure resources, per scope

steps.label: Scope inherits downward
steps.sub: an eligible assignment at a management group applies to every subscription beneath it

code:
# One-time audit:
#   "Who currently holds this role?"
#
# PIM access review (recurring, e.g. quarterly):
#   reviewer must explicitly approve or deny
#   each eligible assignment's CONTINUED existence
#
# Catches: eligible access from a finished project
# that nobody actively cancelled.
caption: PIM also raises its own alerts for roles assigned outside of PIM entirely.
